aspects.says: In comments mode a space written in the pattern is ignored, so a space to be matched is written as \\s or [ ].
basis: section:A Regex in a Text Block Keeps Its Line Breaks, So It Needs Comments Mode

aspects.says: A text block fixture ends its lines with \n and has an exact final newline, so against text from a file or another program compare lines when the format ignores line endings, without ignoring other characters.
basis: section:A Text Block Fixture Has `\n` Line Endings, So Compare Lines When the Format Doesn't Care

aspects.says: A value formatted into a SQL text block becomes part of the statement, quotes around %s included; with a ? placeholder the statement text stays constant and the value is bound separately.
basis: section:A Value Formatted Into SQL Becomes SQL; a Bind Parameter Stays a Value

aspects.says: A table or column name can't be a bind parameter, so a user-chosen identifier is taken from a fixed set of names and anything else is refused.
basis: section:A Value Formatted Into SQL Becomes SQL; a Bind Parameter Stays a Value

aspects.says: Values formatted into an HTML or XML text block are escaped first, & before the rest and quotes inside attributes, or they break the document or become markup.
basis: section:HTML and XML Keep Their Quotes in a Text Block, and Every Inserted Value Still Needs Escaping

aspects.says: A placeholder stands only for a value: binding a column name after ORDER BY closes the injection but doesn't sort by that column.
basis: section:A Value Formatted Into SQL Becomes SQL; a Bind Parameter Stays a Value

aspects.says: A regex laid out over the lines of a text block matches its line breaks, spaces and notes literally unless it is compiled in comments mode.
basis: section:A Regex in a Text Block Keeps Its Line Breaks, So It Needs Comments Mode

aspects.says: A text block's lines end with \n on every platform, while a file checked out with core.autocrlf=true ends them with \r\n.
basis: section:A Text Block Fixture Has `\n` Line Endings, So Compare Lines When the Format Doesn't Care
